title: ICLR 2026 notes — KV caching, MoE inference, and quantization takeaways
content:
Quick brain dump from ICLR 2026 sessions I caught (half remote, half recorded). Mostly thinking about what maps to Redwood serving runtime and low-effort experiments to prioritize. Notes are messy — TODOs at the bottom.

Session: "Efficient Long-Context KV Caching with Sparse Eviction" (poster + short talk)
- Key idea: keep a compact fingerprint index (8-16 bytes per KV) in CPU memory to cheaply decide cache hits before GPU KV loads. Eviction policy mixes LRU with sequence-aware heuristics (favor recent prefixes + per-user TTL).
- Measured: 2–4× fewer GPU KV transfers, 5–12% lower p99 latency on long-span chat traces.
- Implementation notes relevant to Redwood: we can add a lightweight TTL/fingerprint layer in front of existing prefix cache in serving runtime instead of full rewrite. Good fit for dedicated & private where network/hop costs matter.
- Risks: additional memory overhead and consistency complexity for multi-replica setups (stale fingerprints). Need to evaluate how this interacts with our batching pipeline.

Session: "MoE at Inference: Fast Router Fallbacks and Cost-Aware Sparsity"
- Paper proposes deterministic fallback routing: when capacity or router latency is high, switch to a compact dense subnetwork (same model family) via adapter layers. Router uses a cheap confidence estimator to decide route sampling budget.
- For Redwood Dedicated, this could enable graceful degradation: maintain a small dense variant of each MoE model (quantized) and route when GPU pool overloaded. Lower engineering lift than cross-model fallbacks.
- Interesting metric: end-to-end token cost vs. semantic drift (BLEU/ROUGE drops). They reported low semantic drift for many tasks if adapter layers are well-tuned.

Session: "Quantization-aware Kernel Selection"
- Compiler/runtime picks kernels not only by model shape but by quantization profile (8-bit, 4-bit, mixed). Heuristic table grows fast — authors use a tiny NN to predict best kernel given hardware counters and sequence-length distribution.
- Suggests adding a lightweight profiler in Redwood's compile stage that runs microbenchmarks on newly onboarded hardware variants and stores a compact predictor. Could reduce cold-start perf variance.

Other notes / random takeaways
- Posters on token-level caching for code models: fine-grained cache invalidation around edits, good for low-latency coding assistants. Could map to our function-calling + editing workflows.
- Several groups emphasize "prefix-preservation" in batching — ensure KV cache alignment across batched requests so cache reuse stays high.
- Observability: demoed a tracer that emits per-token cache-hit metadata aggregated per-request; very helpful to diagnose cache regressions. Connects well with Redwood Console.

Thoughts on experiments to run (low-effort -> high-value ordering)
1) Fingerprint prefilter prototype (CPU small-index) behind current prefix cache — measure GPU KV transfer counts and p99 latency on our Triage chat trace (use RED-DS-2025-#3). Target: 20% KV transfer reduction. (Owner: Jordan)
2) MoE fallback prototype: pick one small MoE model, train a compact dense adapter, and simulate router overload scenarios with our traffic replay tool. Measure semantic drift and cost savings. (Owner: Priya)
3) Microkernel profiler: add a nightly job that runs tiny GEMM kernels for each hw variant (A100, H100, T4) and stores perf numbers; build a brute-force lookup first, then NN predictor if beneficial. (Owner: Ethan)

Open questions / things to vet
- How much extra memory for fingerprints before we hit undesirable swap behavior on large private deployments? Need a capacity calc for 1M active prefixes.
- Consistency model for fingerprinted cache across replicas — can we accept eventual consistency? What are SLA implications?
- For MoE fallback, licensing/packaging implications if we keep two model variants per customer (dense + MoE). Sales/PS needs a note.

References I want to re-read before prototyping:
- arXiv:2601.01234 — sparse eviction + fingerprint index (poster)
- arXiv:2512.04567 — MoE deterministic routing and adapter fallbacks
- GitHub repro: redwood-inference/repro-kv-experiments (PR/7 has sample implementation)

Action items (short)
- [ ] Spin up fingerprint prefilter PoC on dev cluster (small mem config). Create ticket: JIRA-RED-3421.
- [ ] Sync with Product about MoE fallback packaging and pricing implications (sync 2026-03-15).
- [ ] Add tiny-kernel nightly profiler to infra/benchmarks pipeline (create RFC).
- [ ] Add cache-hit tracer fields to Console schema proposal (draft doc link TBD).

Notes-to-self: keep the initial prototypes lightweight — aim for measurable perf deltas in 2–3 sprints. Share an internal slide deck summarizing findings, include simple cost/value plots (tokens saved vs. additional RAM).

Scratch/links for later:
- Quick grep: `git grep fingerprint` in repro repo for starting point.
- Slack: #kv-cache-discuss for coordination.
- Possible eval dataset: triage-chat-longcontext-2025 (50k tokens per convo)

End of dump. Will iterate and clean up after prototypes show results.
